candidates.exact_span: toxicity tests conducted on effluent discharges where no receiving water is available due to zero flow conditions.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether zero-flow conditions excuse or alter receiving-water toxicity testing affects which monitoring requirements were applicable (B) and whether a no-result or absent test reflects a documented no-discharge period versus unresolved missing evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: If the receiving water is unsatisfactory as a result of instream toxicity (fails to fulfill the test acceptance criteria), the permittee may substitute synthetic dilution water for the receiving water in all subsequent tests
candidates.computation_change_reason: Different readings of when receiving water is 'unsatisfactory' or fails acceptance criteria determine whether substitution is permitted and therefore which monitoring protocol (receiving water vs synthetic dilution water) was actually required for subsequent tests.

candidates.exact_span: a synthetic dilution water control which fulfills the test acceptance require- ments was run concurrently with the receiving water control;
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether this concurrent-control condition was met governs eligibility to use synthetic dilution water; misinterpreting fulfillment of acceptance requirements could change whether subsequent monitoring was required under the substitute protocol or whether reported results lack adequate supporting evidence.

candidates.exact_span: the test indicating receiving water toxicity has been carried out to completion,
candidates.computation_change_reason: What counts as a toxicity test 'carried out to completion' affects whether the permittee satisfied the precondition for substituting synthetic dilution water, changing applicable monitoring obligations (B) and whether incomplete tests are documented no-data versus inadequate evidence (C).

candidates.exact_span: the permittee includes all test results indicating receiving water toxicity with the full report and information required;
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether all required test results and report information were included determines if missing or partial submissions reflect adequately documented evidence versus required monitoring that lacks adequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: the synthetic dilution water shall have a pH, hardness, and alkalinity similar to that of the receiving water or closest downstream perennial water not adversely affected by the discharge, provided the magnitude of these parameters will not cause toxicity in the synthetic dilution water.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of 'similar' parameters, which reference water body applies when receiving water is unsatisfactory, and whether magnitude 'will not cause toxicity' is met affects whether synthetic-dilution substitution was validly invoked and whether associated results constitute adequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall collect two samples (flow-weighted composite if possible) from the outfall(s).
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether two samples are mandatory and whether flow-weighted compositing is required versus merely preferred affects the count and type of sampling obligations applicable to each outfall.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee shall collect a second sample (composite samples if possible) for use during the 24-hour renewal of each dilution concentration for each test.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This establishes an additional per-concentration, per-test sampling obligation tied to 24-hour renewals; different interpretations of scope (each dilution concentration, each test) change how many sampling events were required.

candidates.exact_span: the maximum holding time for any effluent sample shall not exceed 36 hours for first use of the sample. The permittee must have initiated the toxicity test within 36 hours after the collection of the last portion of the first composite sample.
candidates.computation_change_reason: How holding time and test-initiation deadlines are measured (first use, last portion collected) affects whether sampling and testing met permit conditions (B) and whether results from older samples count as adequate evidence or must be treated as deficient or unresolved (C).

candidates.exact_span: Samples shall be chilled to 6 degrees Centigrade during collection, shipping, and/or storage. A holding time up to 72 hrs is allowed upon notification to EPA and NMED of the need for additional holding time.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether chilling to 6°C was satisfied and whether extended holding up to 72 hours was properly notified and allowed changes whether procedural monitoring conditions were met (B) and whether associated test evidence is valid or must be classified as inadequate or unresolved (C).

candidates.exact_span: The permittee must collect the composite samples such that the effluent samples are representative of the discharge duration, and of any periodic episode of chlorination, biocide usage or other potentially toxic substance discharged on an intermittent basis.
candidates.computation_change_reason: What sampling interval and episode coverage satisfies 'representative of the discharge duration' and captures intermittent chlorination, biocide, or other toxic episodes affects required sampling design (B) and whether absent or sparse results reflect conditional non-requirement, documented no-data, or missing required evidence (C).
